condition: when the instructor wants to bring authentic energy into the session

statement: Use a few minutes before class to initiate brief individual conversations and deliberately reach every learner over the term.
condition: when informal pre-class contact is feasible and welcome
exception: respect learners who signal a preference not to converse

statement: Deliberate individual contact can improve the perceived classroom atmosphere and may broaden participation.
condition: when attention extends beyond the learners who already sit near or approach the instructor

statement: Careful instructor attention to learner work communicates that both the work and the person producing it matter.
condition: when feedback demonstrates genuine reading and response

statement: Instructor attention to writing can motivate greater learner effort, which can yield rapid improvement.
condition: in the institution and feedback-rich context studied
exception: attention does not replace instruction in the target skill

statement: Use peripheral course moments to notice individual learners without displacing core instructional time.
condition: when motivation and social connection need strengthening

statement: Write course policies in an empathetic, inviting tone that explains their learning purpose and encourages learners to seek help.
condition: when drafting syllabi and assignment documents
exception: warmth does not require removing necessary standards or consequences

statement: Learners who read a warm-toned syllabus reported greater willingness to ask the instructor for help than learners who read a cold-toned version.
condition: in the syllabus-reading experiment described
exception: reported willingness is not the same as observed help-seeking or learning improvement

statement: Frame a technology policy as a shared attention challenge and explain how the policy supports attention to peers and course material.
condition: when regulating devices in a learning environment

statement: Invite learners to disclose privately when an accommodation or other need conflicts with a course policy and commit to appropriate modification.
condition: when applying a general course policy
exception: follow institutional accommodation processes and do not solicit unnecessary medical detail

statement: Audit course documents for commands and consequence-only language that can be rewritten with rationale, empathy, and a route for concerns.
condition: before the next course begins

statement: Account for learners as whole people whose lives and emotions can affect task performance, and let that awareness shape feedback and policy tone.
condition: when responding to difficulty or nonperformance
exception: compassion should coexist with clear expectations and appropriate boundaries

statement: Shift the central planning question from how the instructor will teach to how the instructor will help particular people learn.
condition: when framing teaching as a scholarly practice

statement: Investigate the teaching-and-learning literature when confronting a recurring classroom problem instead of relying only on personal trial and error.
condition: when relevant scholarship or syntheses are available

statement: Treat helping people learn as a question worthy of sustained scholarly inquiry, not merely a delivery obligation.
condition: when developing professional teaching practice

statement: Continuously adjust teaching to the actual learners in the current course rather than the cohort taught years earlier or a hypothetical average student.
condition: as learner populations and each class community change

statement: Welcome increasingly diverse learners by understanding the knowledge and experience they bring, building community and belonging, and selecting strategies that help them grow from their current position.
condition: when teaching populations with varied backgrounds and needs

statement: Use evidence about human learning to inform teaching experiments without treating evidence as a context-free mechanical recipe.
condition: when translating research into a local course
exception: local creativity and evaluation remain necessary because context affects implementation

statement: Stay current with important developments in learning research because understanding of learning continues to evolve.
condition: when maintaining an evidence-informed teaching practice

statement: Make a small number of deliberate changes to a familiar course to sustain instructor curiosity and professional energy.
condition: when repeated teaching has become routine
exception: do not change so much at once that effects cannot be understood or core course stability is lost

statement: Accept that some teaching experiments will fail and use both successes and failures as evidence for further inquiry.
condition: when trying a bounded instructional change
exception: stop or modify promptly if an experiment creates material learner harm

statement: Instructor satisfaction and enthusiasm are legitimate reasons for ongoing teaching development because they can affect what the instructor brings to learners.
condition: when changes also preserve or improve learner outcomes

statement: Begin a search for teaching guidance with resources curated by established teaching centers or learning experts rather than relying only on a generic web search.
condition: when investigating a specific teaching problem
exception: curated resources should still be assessed for relevance and currency

statement: Select a manageable set of trusted pathways for continuing professional learning instead of trying to master the entire teaching literature.
condition: when the volume of available resources feels overwhelming

statement: Maintain a light recurring learning cadence through a small number of books, podcasts, research updates, or professional events each year.
condition: when sustaining long-term teaching development

statement: Use local teaching-center events to obtain both expert assistance and a peer community for improvement.
condition: when such a center or equivalent faculty-development resource exists

statement: Small teaching changes and large structural innovations are complementary rather than mutually exclusive.
condition: when choosing the scale of pedagogical change

statement: A bounded change can become a low-risk first step toward a larger redesign once experience reveals its broader implications.
condition: when a small experiment exposes a valuable larger opportunity

statement: Expect community-engaged or other large pedagogical redesigns to require partner coordination, new assessments, logistics, and some loss of instructor control.
condition: when moving from a classroom simulation to authentic public or community work

statement: Use different scales of teaching innovation in different courses according to goals, context, capacity, and readiness.
condition: when an instructor teaches multiple distinct courses

statement: Adapt source models and principles to the local course, or use them as prompts to invent a different small strategy when direct transfer does not fit.
condition: when applying teaching guidance to a particular context

statement: Measure a teaching change so it can be refined, retained, or abandoned based on its effects rather than attachment to the idea.
condition: after implementing a bounded instructional change

statement: Use quick midterm surveys, end-of-course feedback, or classroom assessment techniques as proportionate evidence about a teaching change.
condition: when a formal research design is unnecessary or infeasible
exception: self-report alone may not establish actual learning gains

statement: Seek teaching-center support both when implementing a new strategy and when evaluating whether it worked.
condition: when relevant faculty-development expertise is available

statement: Faculty-development teams can use shared recurring teaching challenges as prompts for collaborative small-solution design.
condition: when supporting a local teaching community

statement: Choose an immediate next-class action small enough to implement now rather than postponing all improvement until a future redesign.
condition: when a class meeting is imminent

statement: Use the next course-planning cycle for structural changes such as prior-knowledge activation, cumulative recurrence, synthesis activities, warm policy language, and purpose communication.
condition: when planning a future semester rather than tomorrow's class

statement: Over a teaching career, differentiate strategies by course level and learner need rather than applying every method uniformly.
condition: when experience reveals recurring differences across course contexts

statement: Build a peer group that exchanges teaching ideas and learns jointly from experience and scholarship.
condition: when colleagues are willing to collaborate on improvement

statement: An online course should make the entry point, first task, navigation path, and help routes explicit because students cannot rely on the physical and social cues available in a classroom.
condition: When students enter an online course, especially for the first time

statement: Apparent disengagement in an online course can reflect system barriers and missing social support rather than low motivation or ability.
condition: When learners have difficulty accessing, navigating, or interpreting the online environment

statement: Online course design should account for learners who combine study with employment, caregiving, part-time enrollment, or a return to education after an absence.
condition: When designing for a contemporary online student population

statement: The flexibility that attracts students to online learning can become a liability for learners whose self-regulation skills are still developing.
condition: When a course provides substantial scheduling freedom
exception: Learners with strong self-regulation may benefit from the same flexibility without needing comparable structure

statement: Online instructors should deliberately scaffold organization, planning, time management, help-seeking, and resilience rather than assume students already possess them.
condition: When students need to manage asynchronous learning with limited real-time guidance

statement: Course quality depends on deliberate design and facilitation, not on whether instruction occurs online or in a physical classroom.
Faculty who have little experience as online students often lack the observational models that commonly inform their face-to-face teaching practice.
condition: When instructors have not previously learned in well-designed online courses

statement: Institutions should provide focused professional development and support for online course design and teaching.
condition: When an institution offers or expands online programs

statement: A usable online learning environment should minimize avoidable access and navigation friction before expecting students to engage with academic work.
condition: At initial access and during early course orientation

statement: Online courses need to replace implicit classroom routines with visible instructions and interaction norms.
condition: When learners cannot infer what to do from co-located peers or an instructor's physical presence

statement: Improve teaching through small, actionable changes that can be tested and sustained without rebuilding an entire course.
condition: When a wholesale redesign would be intimidating, risky, or infeasible
exception: A fundamentally broken or newly created course may still require a larger redesign

statement: Large first-pass teaching changes can discourage further innovation when they fail or can prevent instructors from starting because the work appears unmanageable.
condition: When instructors face pressure to overhaul established practice

statement: Teaching changes should be selected using credible evidence about how people learn, not novelty or educational fashion alone.
Universal Design for Learning should be treated as a general course-design framework for diverse learners, not only as an accommodation process for documented disabilities.
Design learning interactions so that common barriers involving time, connectivity, or disability are addressed before an individual must request special treatment.
condition: When foreseeable access barriers can be reduced through course design

statement: Provide more than one practical way for learners to engage with content and demonstrate knowledge when a single format creates avoidable barriers.
condition: When an alternative format can preserve the learning goal
exception: Do not substitute an option that fails to assess the intended learning outcome

statement: Add one useful access or participation option at a time as a manageable way to move toward universal design.
condition: When comprehensive redesign is not immediately practical

statement: Adaptive courseware does not eliminate the need for purposeful human intervention and interaction.
condition: When automated systems personalize content or practice

statement: An asynchronous instructor can be meaningfully present through brief, frequent appearances and learning interventions without being continuously available.
condition: When students may work at any hour
exception: Response-time expectations and urgent-support routes still need to be defined

statement: Evaluate each course run, retain what works, and make targeted design improvements before the next offering.
condition: When the instructor can revise a recurring course
exception: Required coordinated-course elements may constrain what an individual instructor can change

statement: Online communication should be more deliberate because asynchronous settings provide little immediate feedback and few nonverbal cues.
condition: When most interaction is mediated by text or delayed channels
exception: Synchronous audio or video may restore some immediate and nonverbal cues

statement: Use the learning-management system to support learner activity and interaction, not merely to distribute files and grades.
condition: When the platform supports interactive learning functions

statement: Start course planning by identifying why learners are being asked to complete each activity, resource, and assessment.
condition: During course design or revision

statement: Make the purpose of course components visible to online learners because instructors have fewer informal opportunities to reconnect daily work to the larger learning goals.
condition: When learners work through course components asynchronously

statement: Build mechanisms that reveal student progress early enough for the instructor to offer timely guidance and support.
condition: When instructors cannot observe learner confusion directly

statement: Select media and technology by examining what learning purpose each tool serves rather than inheriting or repeating prior tool choices by default.
condition: During online course design or revision
exception: Institutional or coordinated-course constraints may limit the available choices

statement: Try a new teaching activity, observe its effects, refine it, and repeat before judging the approach by its first implementation.
condition: When introducing a manageable, evidence-informed change
exception: Discontinue or redesign promptly if the activity creates material harm or blocks learning

statement: Begin with a systematic, purpose-driven course plan; deliberate structure provides boundaries within which an instructor can still improvise.
condition: When planning a course or substantial unit

statement: Backward design starts by defining the knowledge and capabilities students should retain and use after the course, before selecting content or teaching methods.
condition: During course design or redesign

statement: Write substantive and demonstrable learning outcomes rather than treating objectives as inherited or template-filling language.
condition: When defining the destination for learner development

statement: Design summative assessments to demonstrate achievement of course outcomes and formative assessments to reveal progress toward them.
condition: After the intended learning outcomes are clear

statement: Select content, practice activities, and learning supports only after deciding what students must achieve and how that achievement will be assessed.
condition: During backward course design

statement: Sequence milestones and formative checks so learners make steady progress and receive feedback before a high-stakes assessment.
condition: When learners are preparing for a substantial final performance or product

statement: Align objectives, assessments, activities, and materials so every course component contributes to the intended learning.
Make course alignment visible in several places because sound design that remains implicit can be interpreted by students as disconnected busywork.
condition: In online courses where informal explanation and real-time clarification are limited

statement: Require a low-stakes interaction with the final assessment during the first week so learners understand its purpose, format, and demands early enough to plan.
condition: When a major assessment occurs late in an online course

statement: Merely placing information about a major assessment in a syllabus or nested course folder is insufficient to ensure learners notice and understand it.
condition: When an online course contains many materials and competing demands

statement: Busy online learners may skip optional guidance that carries no accountability, even when it would help them.
condition: When announcements, videos, or feedback are presented as unrequired extras
exception: Some intrinsically motivated learners will engage without an external incentive

statement: Asking learners to attempt a relevant task before they are fully prepared can deepen later learning by prompting generation and closer processing of the eventual answer.
condition: When the attempt is low stakes and followed by instruction or feedback
exception: The early attempt should not be treated as evidence of final mastery

statement: Explain why an early preview or attempt is being assigned so learners can connect the activity to their longer-term success.
condition: When students are asked to engage with work before they feel ready

statement: Open each module with a concise account of what learners will do, why it matters, and which demonstrable goals it advances.
condition: When a course is organized into online modules or units

statement: Reinforce the rationale for current work through short, intentionally timed announcements instead of relying on a single explanation at the start of the course.
condition: During a multiweek online course

statement: Brief, informal instructor videos can communicate relevance and personality effectively without production polish.
condition: When video is a suitable communication channel and an accessible alternative is supplied
exception: Use another concise format when video creates access, bandwidth, or workload barriers

statement: Every instructional video should include captions, a transcript, or an equivalent text-based outline.
condition: When video is used in an online course

statement: Assignment instructions should state the task, its learning purpose, and the process for succeeding, supported where useful by rubrics, checklists, or exemplars.
condition: When assigning online work

statement: Transparent assignment design can reduce procedural questions and improve the quality of evidence students provide about their learning.
condition: When instructions make purpose, expectations, and process clear

statement: Structure reflection to prompt retrieval, elaboration, generation, and planning for future improvement.
condition: When using reflection to strengthen learning

statement: Have learners respond to selected course or module objectives early and periodically; their responses reveal whether the objectives are understood and encourage self-monitoring.
condition: When objective review can be kept brief enough to avoid overload

statement: Allow written, audio, or video reflection options when the response mode is not itself the learning target.
condition: When multiple modes can elicit equivalent evidence of reflection
exception: Require a specific mode when proficiency in that mode is part of the assessed outcome

statement: Conclude a course by asking learners to compare their starting point with their achievements and identify how they will apply or extend the learning.
condition: At the end of a course or substantial learning sequence

statement: Choose private or shared reflection according to whether the goal is individual candor or peer learning and discussion.
condition: When designing a reflective activity

statement: Use recurring explanations of purpose as a design audit: if an activity's contribution to learning cannot be explained, revise or remove it.
condition: When reviewing course content, activities, or assessments

statement: Repeatedly connect current work to core objectives through orientation tasks, module goals, announcements, and feedback.
condition: Throughout an online course

statement: Bookend a course by engaging learners with the final performance near the beginning and asking them to examine their growth at the end.
condition: When a course has a cumulative goal or assessment

statement: Introduce complex performance by separating component skills, teaching foundational elements first, and adding complexity only after learners can manage the earlier layer.
condition: When a task imposes multiple simultaneous cognitive or procedural demands
exception: Learners who demonstrate prerequisite mastery may not need every scaffold

statement: Give learners practice and process-focused feedback on a manageable step before moving them to a harder step.
condition: When skills or assignments build cumulatively

statement: Withholding scaffolding and feedback is not a valid proxy for academic rigor.
condition: When learners are attempting a complex task they have not yet mastered
exception: Scaffolds should be faded when independent performance is the intended outcome

statement: Multiple low-stakes steps, feedback exchanges, and peer-review opportunities can support learning more effectively than requiring only one final submission.
condition: For complex assessments that benefit from iteration
exception: Simple tasks may not warrant a multistage process

statement: Students are more likely to experience an assessment as meaningful when the instructor builds regular engagement into the process of completing it.
condition: When engagement includes useful milestones, instructor feedback, peer review, or preparatory work

statement: Break a complex assignment into an explicit sequence of manageable deliverables with deadlines and a visible process checklist.
condition: When successful completion requires many cognitive or procedural steps

statement: Choose milestone deliverables that expose consequential decisions early, such as a topic, argument, source plan, outline, or draft.
condition: When early correction can prevent later failure
exception: The exact milestone should match the structure of the discipline's task

statement: Review incremental work and return guidance while learners still have enough time to use it.
condition: When a checkpoint is intended to improve a later submission

statement: When many learners make the same serious mistake, first inspect the clarity and design of the instruction rather than attributing the pattern solely to students.
condition: When a substantial portion of a class misunderstands the same requirement

statement: Issue a course-wide correction promptly when a shared misconception would otherwise lead learners to invest more effort in an unworkable direction.
condition: When early submissions reveal a common and consequential misunderstanding
exception: Use individual feedback instead when the problem is isolated or private

statement: Progress checkpoints for group projects can both pace the work and surface collaboration problems before the final submission.
condition: When group work extends over multiple stages
exception: Checkpoints alone do not resolve dysfunctional group dynamics

statement: Conditional release can provide useful structure by requiring evidence of prerequisite understanding before the next learning segment becomes available.
condition: When later content genuinely depends on prior knowledge or performance
exception: Do not gate unrelated content or create barriers that strand learners without a recovery path

statement: In one experimental comparison of entry-level mathematics courses, conditional release improved exam scores and final grades in the online sections but not in the face-to-face sections.
condition: In the studied undergraduate mathematics context
exception: The result should not be generalized automatically to every discipline or course design

statement: A conditional-release checkpoint can serve as nonevaluative feedback and need not always contribute points to the course grade.
condition: When submission, automated feedback, or mastery status itself guides the next action
exception: Assign credit when participation would otherwise be too low or grading is integral to the assessment purpose

statement: Use conditional release selectively because repeated gates can be experienced as obstructive hoops rather than useful scaffolds.
condition: When considering automated progression controls

statement: Every progression gate should provide a clear indication of mastery or a useful route for review and improvement.
condition: When conditional release depends on learner performance

statement: Replace missing visual classroom cues by routinely inspecting learner questions, submissions, and discussion activity for patterns of confusion or disengagement.
condition: When teaching asynchronously or without real-time observation

statement: Use brief, scheduled course check-ins several times across the week rather than relying on infrequent, lengthy visits.
condition: When ongoing online interactions can reveal needs for guidance
exception: The cadence should increase for compressed courses and can decrease for longer-paced formats

statement: When several learners ask the same question, provide a class-wide clarification while also acknowledging the individuals who raised it.
condition: When the answer is useful to the whole class and contains no private information
exception: Respond privately when the issue concerns an individual grade, accommodation, or sensitive circumstance

statement: Maintain a visible course question forum where general questions and answers can benefit all learners.
condition: When the platform supports shared discussion
exception: Provide an equivalent low-barrier channel if public posting is inappropriate or inaccessible

statement: Define and meet a reasonable response cadence for course questions because unanswered posts can leave online learners feeling abandoned.
condition: When learners depend on asynchronous instructor responses to proceed

statement: Convert recurring learner questions into reusable course guidance or a frequently-asked-questions resource for the next offering.
condition: When a question recurs across learners or course runs

statement: An online instructor should participate in discussion forums to guide reasoning, correct misconceptions, and model productive discourse rather than leaving every discussion entirely student-led.
condition: When the forum is intended to advance course learning
exception: Instructor participation should not crowd out peer exchange or turn every thread into instructor approval-seeking

statement: A meta-analysis of online discussions found that students value faculty interaction and that the quality of that interaction can improve peer-to-peer interaction.
condition: Across the online-discussion studies included in the cited meta-analysis
exception: The finding does not prescribe how much instructor participation is optimal in every forum

statement: Discussion responses that accurately summarize a learner's contribution, address its substance, and recur during the week can encourage critical thinking.
condition: In an online discussion designed for substantive learning

statement: At the end of a busy discussion, synthesize the most important ideas, unresolved questions, and exemplary contributions so learners can identify what to retain.
condition: When the volume or complexity of discussion makes key learning hard to discern

statement: Collect discussion highlights while reading posts so the later synthesis is accurate and inexpensive to produce.
condition: When an instructor plans to summarize a module's discussion

statement: Purposefully integrated online discussion can extend engagement between meetings in blended and face-to-face courses as well as in fully online courses.
condition: When between-session interaction supports the course objectives
exception: Do not add a forum that duplicates in-class work without a distinct purpose

statement: Start educational-technology selection with the learning problem or opportunity, then choose the simplest tool that adequately serves the objective.
condition: When selecting or purchasing a tool for teaching
exception: A more complex tool may be warranted when its additional capability is essential to the learning objective

statement: Technology alone does not create active learning; its use must be embedded in a purposeful learning design.
Institutions should pair sophisticated learning spaces or tools with preparation that enables instructors to use them toward clear pedagogical goals.
condition: When deploying unfamiliar or complex educational technology

statement: Multimedia should not be presumed more engaging or effective than plain text; some multimedia designs interfere with learning.
condition: When media adds redundant or poorly coordinated information
exception: Well-aligned multimedia can support objectives that text alone serves less effectively

statement: Do not narrate slide text word for word; coordinate narration closely with the visuals while adding rather than duplicating information.
condition: When recording a narrated slide presentation
exception: Brief verbatim reading may be appropriate for a definition, quotation, or exact wording that itself needs attention

statement: Use conversational language in narrated instructional media.
condition: When narration is intended to explain visual course content
exception: Discipline-specific terminology should remain precise

statement: Prefer short, focused online lecture videos over recordings of full classroom lectures.
condition: When delivering expository content asynchronously
exception: A longer recording may be appropriate when its structure, interaction, or subject matter requires continuity and learners can navigate it

statement: Analysis of millions of viewing sessions supported keeping online instructional videos near six minutes or less and found informal presentation more engaging than high production value.
condition: For the online educational videos represented in the cited viewing dataset
exception: The result is an engagement pattern, not a universal maximum duration for all instructional media

statement: Begin a video library with one short explanation of a concept that has been consistently difficult to teach online, then add more only as experience and need justify them.
condition: When video is likely to solve a specific communication problem

statement: Pair video with accurate captions, a transcript, or a text outline, and verify automatically generated captions before publishing.
condition: When instructional video is provided

statement: Add guiding questions or another small task when learners need help processing a video actively rather than watching passively.
condition: When a video's learning value depends on attention and application

statement: Test that course video is easy to stream and access on the devices learners are likely to use.
condition: Before publishing externally recorded media in an online course

statement: Design reusable instructional videos without term-specific dates and avoid unnecessary dependencies on other videos that make later updates cascade.
condition: When a video may be reused in future course offerings
exception: Use term-specific media when timeliness or cohort context is the instructional purpose

statement: Required instructional media should be paired with a small accountable task that makes learners process or apply its content.
condition: When learners might otherwise treat the media as optional or consume it passively
exception: Accountability may be unnecessary when the media is genuinely optional enrichment

statement: Some busy online learners will skip even useful media when completing it has no explicit relevance or accountability.
condition: When learners are triaging coursework alongside work, family, or other constraints
exception: Learners with sufficient time or intrinsic interest may engage without external accountability

statement: Use automated post-video questions for scalable checks of understanding, with answer feedback that directs learners to a relevant timestamp or extension resource.
condition: When a short objective check is sufficient and class size makes manual review costly
exception: Use a richer response when the goal is interpretation, transfer, or higher-order thinking

statement: Use a brief written, audio, or video response after media when learners need to demonstrate interpretation and application rather than recall alone.
condition: When the educational value of a manually reviewed higher-order response justifies the grading effort
exception: Prefer automated or sampled checks when manual review would be unsustainable

statement: Respond to an emerging class-wide misconception or timely event with a short update that identifies only the salient points learners need next.
condition: When an unplanned teachable moment or shared confusion arises during a course
exception: Use private communication when the matter concerns one learner or sensitive information

statement: A casual video update can restore facial and vocal cues that are absent from text-only online communication.
condition: When meaning or tone benefits from nonverbal communication
exception: An accessible text equivalent must still be available

statement: Allow minor imperfections in instructor-recorded updates when the content remains clear; authentic delivery is preferable to repeated production work that delays useful guidance.
condition: For low-stakes, timely course communication
exception: Correct errors that obscure meaning, undermine accessibility, or convey inaccurate content

statement: Instructors who are uncomfortable on camera can build competence incrementally, beginning with a very short greeting or update.
condition: When video serves a real communication purpose but recording is unfamiliar
exception: Do not force camera use when another medium meets the objective equally well or access and privacy concerns dominate

statement: Curate high-quality existing media when it explains or illustrates a concept better than newly created material, while retaining some instructor-created presence in the course.
condition: When suitable lawful and accessible media already exists
exception: Create original material when course-specific framing or expertise is essential

statement: Include external media only when it advances a learning outcome and addresses a defined instructional need.
condition: When considering a video, audio clip, image, or other media resource

statement: Decorative images, audio, and visuals can overload or confuse learners when they lack a substantive connection to the content.
condition: When multimedia elements compete with rather than support the intended message

statement: Verify copyright and fair-use requirements before incorporating third-party media, using institutional expertise when needed.
condition: When reusing media created by others

statement: Evaluate educational technology by stable pedagogical function and learning purpose rather than by transient product names.
condition: When comparing tools in a rapidly changing technology landscape

statement: Match a tool's affordances to the level of thinking the activity requires, such as remembering, understanding, analyzing, or creating.
condition: When selecting technology for a learning activity

statement: Pilot one minimal use of a new tool, evaluate it, and expand only after instructor and learner experience shows that it works.
condition: When adopting technology beyond established course tools
exception: Urgent accessibility or continuity needs may require a broader initial implementation

statement: A complex technology rollout can create more problems than it solves when users lack preparation or the implementation exceeds the instructional need.
condition: When a large-scale tool implementation is attempted without sufficient fit, support, or testing

statement: Do not require a tool that the instructor cannot use confidently enough to support learners and recover from predictable failures.
condition: When the instructor is responsible for the course implementation
exception: Co-teaching or dedicated technical support may supply the missing operational capacity

statement: New online instructors should first use institutionally supported learning-management tools well before adding external services.
condition: When teaching in a new environment or with unfamiliar tools
exception: Use an external service when a required learning or accessibility function is unavailable in supported tools

statement: Before requiring external technology, assess account creation, subscription cost, assistive-technology compatibility, keyboard access, privacy, and exposure in public spaces.
condition: When a proposed tool operates outside the institution's learning-management system

statement: Usability-test a teaching tool from the learner's perspective so the interface does not consume cognitive resources needed for the learning task.
condition: Before making a technology required

statement: Provide accessible alternatives for media and tools, including accurate captions or transcripts for audio and meaningful text alternatives for images.
condition: When course information or participation depends on media or technology

statement: Accessibility improvements designed for one group can also improve access for others, such as captions supporting both hearing-impaired learners and learners working in another language.
condition: When an alternative representation provides another usable channel for the same content

statement: Online course design should deliberately support relationships among instructor, individual learners, and peers because those people are less visible in asynchronous environments.
condition: When learners often complete coursework in physical isolation

statement: Personal interaction, community, and feedback help learners sustain effort and persist in online study.
condition: When learners lack the regular co-presence and accountability of scheduled classroom meetings

statement: Design online learning so learners can explain, challenge, imitate, and build on one another's thinking rather than interacting only with content.
condition: When social interaction can help learners reach understanding or performance beyond what they can accomplish alone
exception: Independent work remains appropriate when independence is the target or peer interaction would compromise the task

statement: Learners can internalize capabilities first achieved with support from a more experienced person or peers.
condition: When the supported activity lies within reach with appropriate collaboration or guidance
exception: Support cannot substitute for missing prerequisites that place the task far beyond the learner's current capability

statement: Evaluate an online learning community across cognitive presence, social presence, and teaching presence rather than treating course access as equivalent to an educational experience.
condition: When designing or reviewing online learning

statement: Cognitive presence requires sustained communication in which learners reflect, make connections, and remain open to revised understanding.
condition: Within the cited community-of-inquiry framework

statement: Social presence is established when participants can appear as real people through emotional expression, open communication, and group cohesion.
condition: Within the cited community-of-inquiry framework

statement: Teaching presence combines intentional design with active facilitation to support social and cognitive engagement toward learning outcomes.
condition: Within the cited community-of-inquiry framework

statement: Build opportunities and incentives for instructor-learner and peer interaction into the course structure instead of expecting online community to emerge spontaneously.
condition: When learners are separated in time or place

statement: Use an opening peer-introduction activity that also elicits course goals, prior knowledge, or planned learning strategies so community-building immediately serves learning.
condition: At the beginning of an online course
exception: Avoid requiring personal disclosure unrelated to the course

statement: Require a small amount of substantive peer response in an introduction activity so learners begin recognizing one another as collaborators.
condition: When peer community is an intended part of the course
exception: Provide an accessible or private alternative when public interaction creates a material barrier

statement: Use video introductions only when seeing and hearing peers supports the learning or community goal, and provide equitable alternatives.
condition: When audiovisual identity cues would materially strengthen peer recognition
exception: Do not require video when privacy, disability, bandwidth, or the activity's objective makes another mode preferable

statement: Frame discussion prompts around debatable interpretations, cases, persuasion, experience, or application rather than questions with one short closed answer.
condition: When a discussion is meant to produce peer learning
exception: Closed questions remain useful for quick checks of factual understanding

statement: Stagger deadlines for initial contributions and later interaction so peers have material and time for a real asynchronous exchange.
condition: When an online discussion requires interaction over several days

statement: Assess online discussion using criteria tied to timeliness, substantive quality, and meaningful interaction rather than counting posts alone.
condition: When discussion participation contributes to a grade

statement: Do not rigidly require one original post plus a fixed number of replies when an insightful response could better meet the discussion goal than a forced new thread.
condition: When a formulaic participation structure produces inauthentic or low-value exchange
exception: Retain structural minimums when they are needed to ensure broad participation and have demonstrated value

statement: Divide a high-enrollment class into small discussion groups when whole-class volume prevents focused interaction.
condition: When the pedagogical goal is sustained peer exchange and the whole forum is too noisy
exception: Retain whole-class spaces for synthesis or announcements that everyone should share

statement: Choose random, assigned, or self-selected groups according to the interaction goal, such as balanced membership or learner choice of topic.
condition: When configuring small-group online work

statement: Make instructor presence externally visible through frequent, useful, and personal interactions; holding the instructor role does not by itself make learners experience that presence.
condition: In an online course

statement: A case comparison found higher student satisfaction where the instructor posted more often and used names, appreciation, and relevant personal examples in discussion responses.
condition: In the compared sections of one online course
exception: Student satisfaction in a single case is not sufficient evidence of learning gains in every setting

statement: Use announcements to clarify misunderstandings, synthesize recent learning, prepare learners for upcoming work, and maintain course momentum.
condition: When a message applies broadly across the class
exception: Avoid announcements that add noise without a current instructional purpose

statement: Schedule useful announcements in advance to maintain predictable communication during a known absence.
condition: When travel or another commitment will interrupt the instructor's usual posting routine
exception: Scheduled messages should not imply live availability that the instructor cannot provide

statement: Publish a realistic feedback-turnaround expectation and communicate promptly when unusual circumstances will delay it.
condition: When learners submit work for instructor review

statement: Engaged instructor presence is especially important for learners who doubt their academic ability or are at risk of marginalization.
condition: When serving underserved or academically uncertain online learners

statement: Deliberately reveal enough professional and personal identity for online learners to experience the instructor as a real, approachable person.
condition: When instructor and learners do not share a physical space
exception: Maintain appropriate privacy and professional boundaries; personal disclosure is not an end in itself

statement: Design the learner's first course entry to communicate welcome, instructor identity, enthusiasm for the subject, and confidence in the learning ahead.
condition: Before an online course opens

statement: An instructor introduction can combine a concise professional biography with a few relevant interests or experiences rather than presenting credentials alone.
condition: When creating a reusable instructor-introduction page or recording
exception: Avoid disclosures that could pressure learners to reciprocate or distract from the learning relationship

statement: Informal imperfections in an instructor introduction can strengthen authenticity and trust when intelligibility and professionalism remain intact.
condition: For low-stakes introductory or relational media
exception: Repair technical or content defects that impede access, accuracy, or comprehension

statement: Check audio clarity and supply accurate captions or a transcript for instructor-introduction media.
condition: When an introduction includes audio or video

statement: Continue using an authentic instructor voice throughout the term rather than treating human presence as a one-time welcome activity.
condition: Throughout an online course

statement: Account for the ways cultural context can affect participation, communication, self-efficacy, and interpretation in an online course.
condition: When designing and facilitating learning for a culturally diverse population
exception: Do not reduce an individual learner to assumptions about a cultural group

statement: A learner's silence, delayed reply, or discussion behavior should not automatically be interpreted without considering cultural and contextual explanations.
condition: When interpreting online participation patterns
exception: Address persistent nonparticipation when course progress or safety requires intervention

statement: Institutions and instructors should seek development in culturally responsive online teaching rather than assume face-to-face inclusion practices transfer automatically.
condition: When serving diverse online cohorts

statement: Monitor online discussions for derogatory language, patterned exclusion, and unequal response to particular learners.
condition: When learners interact in persistent written or recorded spaces

statement: Intervene when discussion records reveal marginalization by removing harmful content when necessary and modeling inclusive ways to engage across differences.
condition: When learner safety, belonging, or equitable participation is being undermined
exception: Preserve and address difficult but legitimate disagreement when it can be facilitated safely and educationally

statement: Use low-risk activities such as preferred-name and pronunciation sharing to invite cultural awareness while giving learners control over what they disclose.
condition: When community-building activities can respectfully acknowledge identity
exception: Do not compel explanations of names, heritage, or identity

statement: Treat cultural inclusion as a continuing design and facilitation responsibility rather than a single diversity activity.
Design course policies with awareness that online learners may be balancing employment, caregiving, health, financial pressure, and other obligations outside the course.
condition: When setting deadlines, participation expectations, and recovery options
exception: Essential sequencing, safety, accreditation, or collaborative dependencies may limit flexibility

statement: Care in online teaching requires maintaining conditions that welcome and support learners, not merely feeling empathy for them.
Create a bounded, transparent mechanism for deadline extensions, revision, or recovery so ordinary disruptions do not require learners to disclose private hardship.
condition: When limited flexibility can be offered without defeating the learning objective or harming collaborators
exception: Courses with immovable external constraints may need a different recovery mechanism

statement: Track the use of flexible-policy tokens or exceptions consistently so care does not make administration arbitrary.
condition: When learners have a limited number of automatic recovery options

statement: Begin from positive intent when a learner requests help or additional time, while applying the course's stated boundaries and evidence requirements consistently.
condition: When a learner reports an unexpected obstacle
exception: Escalate or verify when policy, safety, equity, or repeated misuse requires it

statement: Contact a disengaged learner before initiating an avoidable administrative withdrawal so the instructor can understand the situation and identify a feasible recovery path.
condition: When direct outreach is permitted and a learner's status is at risk
exception: Follow immediate institutional procedures when safety, legal, or mandatory-drop rules leave no discretion

statement: Use a brief synchronous conversation when tone, misunderstanding, or a complex personal obstacle is difficult to resolve asynchronously.
condition: When both parties can access a phone or videoconference and real-time exchange is likely to help
exception: Offer an asynchronous alternative for accessibility, privacy, scheduling, or time-zone reasons

statement: A scalable personal check-in can identify the small subset of learners who need specific support without requiring intensive intervention for the whole class.
condition: When course-wide energy or participation is unusually low
exception: Use targeted outreach when clear risk signals already identify particular learners

statement: Plan efficient instructor-community practices that can be sustained through the final week rather than front-loading presence and then disappearing as workload grows.
condition: When selecting community-building and communication routines

statement: Return feedback early enough for learners to use it before completing too many subsequent assessments.
condition: When later work depends on the same knowledge or skill
exception: A deliberate short delay may support processing after some high-stakes assessments

statement: A grade without targeted information about strengths and next improvements does not adequately guide learner development.
condition: When the learner will perform related work again
exception: A purely terminal certification decision may offer fewer opportunities to apply developmental feedback

statement: Online courses need explicit routes for asking questions and predictable feedback routines because asynchronous learners cannot rely on scheduled meetings to locate the instructor.
condition: When learners and instructors are not regularly co-present

statement: Instructor presence requires reasonable response and feedback times but does not require continuous availability.
condition: In an asynchronous online course
exception: Institutions may define urgent-response duties for specific safety or clinical contexts

statement: Notify learners in advance of a planned absence and explain how response or grading times will change.
condition: When an instructor expects to be offline beyond the usual response window

statement: Distinguish summative feedback that explains a judgment from formative feedback that tells learners how to improve before a consequential evaluation.
condition: When designing assessment and feedback

statement: Provide frequent, low-stakes opportunities for learners to receive formative feedback rather than concentrating feedback on final graded products.
condition: When skills or understanding can improve through iteration
exception: Not every simple or terminal task needs a separate formative cycle

statement: Fairness, helpfulness, and clear communication in grading influence learners' willingness to engage.
condition: When assessment practices shape learners' perception of instructor interest and support

statement: A cited meta-analysis found immediate feedback more beneficial for low-stakes quizzes and activities, while feedback after a delay was more beneficial for major tests.
condition: Across the assessment contexts included in the cited meta-analysis
exception: The evidence did not establish one universal turnaround interval for every task

statement: Prioritize rapid feedback on short, low-stakes work while allowing enough time to give thoughtful feedback on major assessments.
condition: When grading workload requires differentiated turnaround priorities
exception: Do not delay major-assessment feedback beyond the point where learners can use it

statement: Frame each feedback comment around what the learner needs now to move forward, not merely what was wrong in the completed work.
condition: When giving developmental feedback
exception: Summative decisions still require a clear account of how the completed work met the criteria

statement: Separate feedback into clearly labeled observations about current performance and concrete guidance for the next attempt.
condition: When a submission receives both a judgment and developmental guidance

statement: Set due dates with both learner pacing and the instructor's ability to answer last-minute questions and return timely feedback in mind.
condition: When constructing the course schedule
exception: Externally fixed dates may constrain the schedule

statement: Avoid scheduling a complex, question-generating task during a period when the instructor cannot provide time-sensitive support.
condition: When instructor unavailability is known during course planning
exception: Provide alternate support or comprehensive contingency guidance if the timing cannot change

statement: Align the last support window before a deadline with the times learners are likely to do the work.
condition: When the learner population has predictable work or caregiving patterns
exception: Offer asynchronous guidance when no single support window serves the cohort

statement: Use a short real-time conversation when repeated asynchronous exchanges are failing to resolve confusion or reach a decision.
condition: When learner and instructor can find a mutually accessible time and synchronous exchange is more efficient
exception: Retain an asynchronous option for scheduling, disability, privacy, bandwidth, or time-zone constraints

statement: Do not make a single scheduled synchronous event mandatory for an asynchronous cohort whose work and family schedules differ.
condition: When asynchronous flexibility is a core access feature of the course
exception: A program may require synchronous participation when it was disclosed at enrollment and is essential to the learning outcome

statement: When offering synchronous support, provide multiple times, optional attendance, a recording, or a comparable asynchronous learning experience.
condition: When not every learner can attend the live event
exception: A recording alone may be insufficient when the learning objective depends on active participation; provide an equivalent participatory alternative

statement: Scale individual synchronous conversations according to enrollment and need, reserving them for struggling learners when meeting every student is not feasible.
condition: When one-to-one conversation could improve engagement or understanding
exception: A universal brief meeting may be justified in a small class with high anticipated anxiety

statement: Schedule virtual office-hour sessions at a few high-value points rather than holding frequent sessions that learners rarely attend.
condition: When attendance and value improve through timing near exams, projects, or common feedback needs
exception: Frequent office hours remain appropriate when learner demand supports them

statement: Announce synchronous support well ahead, account for time zones, and solicit questions beforehand so the session addresses real needs.
condition: When planning a live online support session

statement: If live attendance earns credit, offer a comparable credit-bearing task for learners who cannot attend.
condition: When optional synchronous participation is incentivized

statement: Invest upfront in a reusable learning-management-system rubric to reduce repeated grading effort while preserving specific feedback.
condition: When the same criteria will be applied across many submissions or course runs
exception: A rubric may be unnecessary for highly individualized work that cannot be meaningfully represented by common criteria

statement: Make the rubric visible before submission so learners can see the standards used to evaluate their work.
condition: When a rubric defines assessment expectations
exception: Withhold scoring details only when advance disclosure would invalidate the assessment, while still communicating relevant criteria

statement: Align rubric criteria and performance descriptions closely with assignment instructions and intended learning outcomes.
condition: When designing or revising a rubric

statement: Consider audio or video feedback when vocal tone, facial expression, or visual walkthrough would convey encouragement and nuance that written comments may lose.
condition: When the medium is accessible to the learner and adds value to the feedback
exception: Use text when it is easier to review, search, access, or apply to precise edits

statement: The cited comparisons did not find a significant performance advantage for audio feedback over written feedback.
condition: In the biology, composition, and related course contexts represented by the cited studies
exception: The absence of a measured performance difference does not rule out relational, motivational, or contextual benefits

statement: Students in the cited studies generally perceived audio feedback as more personal, useful, and detailed than written comments.
condition: Among respondents in the cited feedback studies
exception: Preference for audio should not be assumed for every learner

statement: Audio feedback may take longer to create than written comments while still delivering substantially more explanation in that time.
condition: When instructors speak comments more fully than they would type them
exception: Production time may fall with practice, and concise written feedback may be more efficient for some tasks

statement: Use recorded feedback to combine acknowledgment of effort, a supportive tone, and unambiguous direction about what must improve.
condition: When learners may be anxious and the task is challenging
exception: Supportive delivery must not blur the substantive performance standard

statement: Start with audio feedback before attempting video or screen-capture feedback when recording is a new skill and technical simplicity matters.
condition: When the instructor wants to pilot media feedback with minimal preparation
exception: Begin with screen capture when visually pointing to the work is essential to understanding the comments

statement: Choose feedback technology for its ability to deliver targeted guidance efficiently, not merely because the medium is novel.
condition: When deciding among text, rubric, audio, video, screen capture, or a live conversation

statement: Reduce learner uncertainty by clearly showing how current performance compares with expectations and what action would improve it.
condition: When feedback is intended to sustain effort and self-efficacy

statement: Academic rigor is compatible with encouragement, mentoring, and embedded support; supporting persistence does not require lowering content or inflating grades.
condition: When learners face difficult or unfamiliar work

statement: Orient anxious beginners by explaining what to expect, how support will work, and why success is feasible with appropriate practice.
condition: When learners are entering an unfamiliar or intimidating learning context
exception: Do not promise success independent of required effort and performance

statement: Point out specific evidence of learner progress so encouragement is grounded in demonstrated development rather than empty praise.
condition: When learners are struggling to recognize their own improvement

statement: Believing that ability can improve can support persistence, but mindset interventions have meaningful limits and should not be treated as a universal cure.
condition: When learners encounter challenge and have access to viable strategies and support
exception: A mindset message cannot remove structural barriers, discrimination, poverty, or inaccessible course conditions

statement: Do not use growth-mindset language to shift responsibility for structural inequity or poor course design onto learners.
condition: When explaining persistence or performance gaps

statement: Praising effort alone is insufficient; learners also need opportunities to change strategies, seek input, reflect, and focus effort on improvement.
condition: When an initial approach has not produced learning

statement: Build strategy trials, help-seeking, and reflection into course structure rather than relying only on motivational messages about persistence.
condition: When designing support for learner persistence

statement: Published estimates cited in the book place online-course attrition above face-to-face attrition, but the magnitude varies widely and recent national evidence was limited.
condition: For the higher-education studies and period discussed by the authors
exception: The cited estimates should not be treated as a current universal rate for all institutions or course types

statement: Check objective early-course signals such as access, participation, or first-assessment performance and contact at-risk learners while behavior can still change.
condition: When the course provides reliable indicators of a weak start
exception: Do not treat an automated risk signal as proof of ability, intent, or personal circumstances

statement: Write an early nudge in a supportive, nonblaming tone that identifies the observed issue, asks learners to examine their preparation, points to support, and expresses confidence in improvement.
condition: When contacting a learner after an early sign of difficulty
exception: Escalate more directly when immediate safety, academic-integrity, or administrative action is required

statement: Personalize a scalable nudge with the learner's name and observed situation even when the core guidance is templated.
condition: When several learners need similar early outreach
exception: Do not expose one learner's performance to others or imply individualized analysis that did not occur

statement: In a cited controlled study, students who received two personalized support-reminder emails earned higher grades than the control group.
condition: In the educational context examined by that study
exception: The result does not establish that every email nudge or learner population will produce the same effect

statement: At the start of an online course, require learners to turn general intentions into a concrete plan for managing the course's workload, schedule, and support routes.
condition: When self-directed planning is important to course completion
exception: Do not impose a redundant planning task on learners who already demonstrate an adequate plan through another activity

statement: A learning contract should state realistic course expectations such as weekly effort, participation cadence, deadlines, question channels, and available help.
condition: When learners may lack experience estimating the demands of an online course
exception: Expectations must be evidence-based and appropriate to the actual course rather than copied from a generic template

statement: A signature or checkbox alone may produce superficial compliance rather than thoughtful commitment.
condition: When learners can complete an agreement mechanically in order to unlock course access
exception: An agreement can still document expectations even if it does not itself cause reflection

statement: Make a learning contract reflective by asking each learner to name goals, a committed action, an anticipated obstacle, and a strategy for overcoming it.
condition: When using a beginning-of-course commitment activity

statement: Allow learners to articulate a goals plan in writing or an equivalent recording when the response mode is not the learning target.
condition: When either mode can produce the same reflective evidence
exception: Require a particular mode when proficiency in it is an intended outcome

statement: Revisit the learner's initial goals and plan at strategic points so setbacks lead to revised action rather than abandonment.
condition: During a course long enough for plans and circumstances to change

statement: Use a mastery quiz to verify genuinely prerequisite knowledge before learners proceed to dependent content.
condition: When later learning requires a clearly defined baseline of concepts or vocabulary
exception: Do not gate progression on material that is not essential to the next task

statement: Set the mastery threshold according to the prerequisite risk and content rather than assuming every quiz must require a perfect score.
condition: When configuring a mastery requirement
exception: Require complete accuracy when every item represents nonnegotiable safety or foundational knowledge

statement: Permit enough low-stakes attempts for learners to diagnose and close knowledge gaps before a mastery gate becomes final.
condition: When a quiz is designed for learning and progression rather than one-shot certification
exception: Limit attempts when item security, safety, or the validity of the assessment requires it

statement: A mastery checkpoint can be excluded from the final grade when its purpose is to establish readiness rather than rank performance.
condition: When successful completion is already required to progress
exception: Award credit when the effort is substantial or grading is needed to sustain equitable participation

statement: Embed actionable feedback in each mastery-quiz response, directing a learner to the precise resource needed to reconsider an incorrect answer.
condition: When automated feedback can guide self-remediation
exception: Provide human support when repeated attempts show that resource directions are insufficient

statement: Use correct-answer feedback to extend learning with optional related resources rather than limiting feedback to remediation.
condition: When an extension will not distract from required progress
exception: Keep feedback concise when additional material would create overload

statement: Repeated mastery attempts can prompt learners to reflect on what they do not know and practice study behaviors needed to close the gap.
condition: When attempts include informative feedback and access to relevant study resources
exception: Unguided repetition can become guessing rather than learning

statement: Structure an early task so learners can succeed while practicing only a limited set of component skills needed for a later complex performance.
condition: When a final task combines several unfamiliar technical or cognitive demands
exception: Learners who demonstrate the component skills may move to a more advanced scaffold

statement: Early, repeated successes can strengthen self-efficacy, while repeated early failures can lower expectations of future mastery.
condition: During the early development of a skill
exception: Occasional later failure may have less effect after robust self-efficacy has been established

statement: Increase task complexity gradually across a sequence of practice opportunities rather than assigning the full performance after only a distant warning.
condition: When learners are acquiring a new multistep skill
exception: A diagnostic full-task attempt may be useful when it is low stakes and followed by scaffolding

statement: Give feedback on each scaffolded performance before the next, more difficult version is due.
condition: When successive tasks are meant to build the same skill

statement: Use low-stakes, good-faith completion criteria for an initial scaffold when the main purpose is confidence and procedural practice rather than polished performance.
condition: At the first attempt of an unfamiliar skill
exception: Assess accuracy immediately when mistakes create safety risks or reinforce harmful misconceptions

statement: Use strong structure to help learners develop self-direction, then expect increasing responsibility as they gain competence.
condition: When learners initially lack routines for managing online study
exception: Do not preserve scaffolds that prevent the independent performance the course intends to develop

statement: Motivation is shaped by both perceived control over important learning activity and perceived value of that activity.
condition: Within the cited control-value theory of achievement emotions
exception: Control and value are not the only influences on motivation or learning

statement: Give learners bounded choices that let them connect required learning to their own academic, professional, or personal goals.
condition: When multiple paths can satisfy the same course outcomes
exception: Do not offer choices that bypass essential outcomes or create inequivalent assessment demands

statement: A curriculum that serves learners with materially different career goals should provide relevant pathways rather than force everyone through one context-specific application.
condition: When shared program outcomes can be achieved through distinct authentic contexts
exception: A common application remains necessary when it is itself a required professional competency

statement: Choice is most motivating when it increases meaningful control without removing the structure needed for online success.
condition: When designing learner autonomy
exception: Unbounded choice can overburden learners who lack sufficient knowledge or planning skills

statement: Create conditions in which learners can exercise agency rather than attempting to confer agency through motivational language alone.
condition: When course design can give learners meaningful control over how they direct effort

statement: Autonomy combines meaningful control with responsibility for directing one's own learning.
condition: In the educational sense used by the authors
exception: Autonomy does not mean the absence of instructor guidance or course requirements

statement: Balance learner freedom with expert guidance by defining nonnegotiable outcomes and supports while leaving meaningful decisions to learners.
condition: When designing for autonomy
exception: More guidance is warranted when learners lack prerequisite knowledge to make a productive choice

statement: Students in the cited meaningful-writing research valued both agency in their work and guidance from instructors.
condition: Across the student accounts in the cited project
exception: The finding does not specify one optimal freedom-to-guidance ratio for every learner or task

statement: Offer several discussion topics that all advance the module outcomes, allowing learners to pursue the question they find most relevant.
condition: When an online discussion can meet its goal through more than one prompt
exception: Use a common prompt when comparison of the same problem is essential

statement: Let learners select a subset from a curated collection and teach one another about their selections when collective coverage can replace universal reading.
condition: When no single item is required prerequisite knowledge for every learner
exception: Require common core resources that everyone must understand

statement: Include discussion options that invite learners to connect course concepts with their own work, experience, or decision-making.
condition: When personal application can be shared without compelled sensitive disclosure
exception: Offer a nonpersonal analytical option for learners who do not wish to disclose experience

statement: Judge a discussion contribution by substance and learning value rather than the number of prompts it addresses.
condition: When learners can choose among prompts
exception: Breadth requirements remain appropriate when comparing multiple perspectives is an explicit outcome

statement: When the communication mode is not the outcome, allow learners to choose between equivalent written and recorded discussion contributions.
condition: When both modes can support the same substantive interaction
exception: Require a specific mode when practicing it is part of the learning objective

statement: Choice in activities and assignments has been associated with greater completion, interest, enjoyment, and perceived competence.
condition: When the choices are meaningful and remain aligned with learning goals
exception: Excessive or poorly structured choice can fail to produce these benefits

statement: Allow learners to self-enroll in project groups by topic interest when all topics provide equivalent learning value.
condition: When interest-based group membership is feasible and group capacity is managed
exception: Assign groups when equity, balance, accessibility, or the learning goal requires a different composition

statement: Use online group work only when collaboration serves an authentic pedagogical purpose rather than treating teamwork as automatically valuable.
condition: When considering a collaborative assignment
exception: Learners with substantial workplace or military collaboration experience may reasonably find generic teamwork practice forced and unnecessary

statement: An effective online collaborative project should have a clear learning purpose, a structured team-building start, a conflict process, transparent communication, and explicit grading criteria.
condition: When assigning asynchronous group work

statement: Design team roles so contributions are genuinely interdependent and individual strengths help the group meet a shared objective.
condition: When roles are used in a collaborative task
exception: Avoid artificial roles that fragment a task without requiring collaboration

statement: Have teams negotiate expectations, respectful behavior, communication, and a process for handling missed commitments before substantial project work begins.
condition: For extended online group projects
exception: A lightweight shared protocol may suffice for brief, low-dependency collaboration

statement: Require periodic group progress reports so teams can hold themselves accountable and problems become visible before the deadline.
condition: When a collaborative project spans multiple stages

statement: Apply specifications grading selectively to tasks whose acceptable performance can be expressed through clear, nonnegotiable criteria.
condition: When a submission can be judged meaningfully as meeting or not meeting a defined standard
exception: Do not force binary grading onto nuanced work whose quality cannot be reduced to defensible specifications

statement: Specifications grading can hold learners to a high minimum standard while reducing time spent distinguishing arbitrary near-adjacent percentages.
condition: When the specifications and threshold are clear and efficiently checkable
exception: It does not remove the need to design valid criteria or give developmental feedback

statement: Define discussion quality through substantive contribution to the conversation, not arbitrary word-count bands.
condition: When specifications grading is used for discussion
exception: A length guideline may still help communicate an approximate scope

statement: Pair all-or-nothing specifications grading with a limited opportunity to revise, resubmit, or recover from an honest mistake.
condition: When a first failure would otherwise make the binary standard disproportionately punitive
exception: Recovery may be restricted for academic-integrity violations or irreversible safety-sensitive performance

statement: A bounded recovery token can preserve high standards while acknowledging that disruptions and honest errors occur.
condition: When learners know the token rules and the work can still be completed validly

statement: Make the syllabus an active learning resource by inviting learners to annotate policies, assignments, expectations, questions, and advice.
condition: At course orientation and as questions arise
exception: Protect private questions and prevent annotation from changing nonnegotiable institutional requirements

statement: Preserve syllabus annotations as a shared question-and-answer record that learners can revisit during the term.
condition: When the annotation platform remains accessible to the cohort

statement: Course co-design can include learner input on readings, activities, assignments, or pathways, but it requires sustained instructor responsiveness and should be scoped realistically.
condition: When institutional requirements and course outcomes permit meaningful adaptation
exception: Do not imply negotiability for safety, accreditation, legal, or essential outcome requirements

statement: Pilot co-design by leaving one bounded learning objective or assessment pathway for learners to define rather than redesigning the whole course at once.
condition: When an instructor wants to introduce learner co-creation incrementally
exception: The learner-defined element must remain compatible with the course's essential outcomes

statement: Use a familiar annotation tool when it can support discussion of the syllabus; learning a new platform should not displace the pedagogical purpose.
condition: When selecting technology for syllabus annotation or co-design
exception: A new tool is justified when familiar options cannot provide an essential function

statement: Provide substantial early support for online learners and deliberately fade it as they demonstrate greater independence.
